title: Principle of Least Privilege
description: Deny access by default and grant only the minimum permissions required for authorised accounts or processes to perform a specific function based on the account inventory implemented.
guidance: Consider attribute- or feature-based access control for customization and granularity. Suggested tools include AWS IAM Access Advisor or Azure AD Access Review. Risk: Violating least privilege principles increases risk of unauthorized access, privilege escalation, and security breaches due to unnecessary permissions.

title: Identity and Device-Based Access Control
description: Adopt Identity and Device-Based Access Control for secure and context-aware connectivity to private organisational resources.
guidance: Use solutions like Secure Service Edge (SSE), Identity Aware Proxies (IAP), or Zero Trust services (Entra ID Conditional Access, Okta Device Trust) integrating identity and device management. Risk: Relying on direct connections or traditional VPNs without strong identity and device-based measures increases risk of unauthorized access and data breaches.

title: Single User Endpoints
description: Assign each endpoint device to a single designated primary [ac-11_prm_1] and enforce the assignment to ensure accountability and enhance security monitoring.
guidance: Implement user authentication and endpoint management with device enrollment. For secondary support accounts, consider endpoint privilege management tools. Risk: Multiple users accessing a single endpoint can lead to data leakage, activity tracking difficulties, and increased insider threat vulnerability.

title: Single Sign-On (SSO) for Internal Services and Accounts
description: Use Single Sign-On (SSO) for internal services and accounts.
guidance: Configure multi-factor authentication at the SSO identity provider, ensuring access is granted only after IdP user authentication. Risk: Without SSO, there is increased risk of unauthorized access and compromised credentials, as users may resort to weak or reused passwords across systems.

title: Static Credential Expiry and Rotation
description: Rotate long-lived static credentials such as API keys, access keys, and personal access tokens every [ac-13_prm_1] day(s) or use time-restricted credentials.
guidance: Automate credential rotation where possible. Consider time-restricted alternatives like AWS Security Token Service and IAM Identity Center instead of IAM user access keys. Risk: Failure to regularly rotate long-lived credentials increases risk of unauthorized access from stolen or unrevoked credentials.

title: Inventory of Accounts
description: Establish and maintain an inventory of all accounts and their access rights managed within the system.
guidance: Regularly review and update the account inventory for accuracy and completeness. Implement automated tools where feasible to track and manage accounts and access rights. Risk: Failure to maintain accurate account inventory increases risk of unauthorized access, account misuse, and security breaches.

title: Validation Testing of Automated Account Lifecycle Management
description: Conduct validation tests on the system integrated with account management tools to ensure secure integration.
guidance: Test cases should verify provisioning occurs solely through management tools, accounts deactivate on final authorization day, provisioning follows access permission validation, and access rights match assigned roles and functions. Risk: Failure to validate account management tool integration increases risk of unauthorized access, improper provisioning, and security breaches.

title: Separation of Duties
description: Implement and maintain separation of duties for access and privileges to prevent any single individual from having excessive control over key processes or systems.
guidance: Implement multiple controls including role-based access control (RBAC), Privileged Identity Management (PIM), and Just-In-Time access. Use compensating controls like audit logging, alerting, and rate limits. Consider Azure AD PIM or AWS Organizations. Risk: Failure to implement separation of duties increases risk of fraud, errors, and system misuse due to privilege concentration.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
description: Require MFA for privileged accounts at login.
guidance: Authentication factors should be different and independent of the accessing device. Consider MFA for privileged actions at the application level using PIM tools. Risk: Without phishing-resistant MFA for remote access, there is increased risk of unauthorized access, credential theft, and compromise of sensitive systems.

title: Inactive and Expired Accounts
description: Disable or remove [ac-3_prm_3] accounts within [ac-3_prm_1] day(s) from last day of authorised use or have not been used for [ac-3_prm_2] day(s).
guidance: Use automated checks to identify accounts needing disabling. Consider SCIM or identity lifecycle management tools. For cloud, use tools like AWS Config iam-user-unused-credentials-check. Risk: Failure to disable unused accounts with elevated access increases risk of unauthorized access and exploitation.

title: Access Review
description: Perform an access review [ac-4_prm_1] and remove unauthorised or unnecessary access rights within [ac-4_prm_2] day(s).
guidance: For applications, implement automated review workflows or reports. For cloud accounts, use AWS IAM Access Advisor or Azure AD Access Review. Risk: Without regular access reviews, there is increased risk of lingering access, privilege misuse, and compromised security.

title: Endpoint Device Hardening
description: Require hardened endpoint devices for remote developer, maintainer, or administrator access.
guidance: Use Endpoint Management platforms to continuously check and enforce device security posture, denying access if hardening requirements are unmet. Risk: Without hardened endpoints for remote access, there is increased risk of compromised endpoints, malware infections, and unauthorized system access.

title: Default Credentials
description: Change default credentials prior to first use.
guidance: Identify default credentials in system components before deployment and change them. Configure end-user systems to prompt for password change on first login after account creation. Risk: Failure to change default credentials increases risk of unauthorized access, as these are well-known and targeted by attackers.

title: Singpass/Corppass for Public Users
description: Use Singpass or Corppass MFA for digital services that require high level of identity assurance for Public Users.
guidance: For high-impact or high-risk transactions, use Singpass/Corppass to identify public users. Agency/internal users should use Government-managed SSO (such as WOG AAD). Leverage Singpass/Corppass to reduce duplication and provide consistent user experience.

title: Automated Account Lifecycle Management
description: Automate account [ac-8_prm_1] for [ac-8_prm_3] using an account lifecycle management tool.
guidance: Consider adopting SSO with just-in-time provisioning or tools such as [ac-8_prm_2]. Perform validation testing to ensure timely provisioning/deprovisioning. Configure systems to enhance capabilities via automation. Risk: Manual account lifecycle management introduces errors and weaknesses, making access control measures ineffective.

title: Endpoint Device Management
description: Implement and maintain an endpoint device management solution to ensure the security and integrity of endpoint devices used within the organisation.
guidance: Mobile Device Management (MDM) platforms enable management, monitoring, and secure configuration, including disk encryption, configuration management, regular updates, and remote data wiping capabilities. Risk: Unmanaged endpoint devices increase risk of unauthorized access and loss of sensitive information.

title: Input Validation
description: Validate all application inputs to ensure that they match the expected type, structure, or format.
guidance: Strictly validating inputs against a comprehensive schema prevents injection attacks caused by inserting special characters or content that would cause the application to perform incorrect operations. Risk: Without input validation, there's a heightened risk of injection attacks, data manipulation, or system crashes due to unexpected input, potentially leading to unauthorised access or disruption of services.

title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
description: Set HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) response headers with a maximum age value of at least 1 year (31536000 seconds) to mitigate protocol downgrade attacks.
guidance: Refer to the OWASP Secure Headers Project Best Practices for recommended header values. Risk: Failure to implement HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) with a sufficient maximum age may expose the system to protocol downgrade attacks, compromising the security of communication channels.

title: Session Management
description: Require [ insert: param, as-11_prm_2 ] to re-authenticate after their session exceeds [ insert: param, as-11_prm_1 ] hour(s) or terminate the session.
guidance: NIST SP 800-63B recommends re-authentication once per 30 days for Authenticator Assurance Level 1, 12 hours or 30 minutes inactivity for Authenticator Assurance Level 2, and 12 hours or 15 minutes inactivity for Authenticator Assurance Level 3. In addition to time period, system can consider re-authentication when roles, authenticators or credentials change or when the execution of privileged functions occurs. Risk: Not re-authenticating regularly and at suitable checkpoints could allow someone who has access to the account to carry out unauthorised actions.

parameters.description: The maximum time period in hours of a user's session.

title: Malware Scanning of Uploaded Files
description: Scan file uploads for malware before further processing by the system.
guidance: Consider uploading the files to temporary storage for malware scanning on ephemeral compute like serverless functions before moving safe files to another storage for further processing or unsafe files to quarantine storage. Risk: Without scanning uploaded files for malware, there's an increased risk of exploits or infection for consumers of the files.

title: Exposure of Internal System Details
description: Prevent the unnecessary disclosure of internal system details to Public Users.
guidance: Ensure all system messages and notifications are informative yet secure. These messages should be contextually appropriate, providing relevant information without exposing internal system details such as debug information, stack traces, or software versioning. Risk: Disclosure of internal system details or debug stack traces can expose vulnerabilities, software versions, and system architecture, potentially leading to targeted attacks, exploitation of known vulnerabilities, and unauthorised access to sensitive systems or data.

title: Secure Cryptographic Libraries
description: Use reputable and secure cryptographic libraries and functions to handle cryptographic operations.
guidance: Follow the OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet for best practices in securely implementing cryptographic operations. Regularly update libraries and prefer widely recognised ones such as OpenSSL. Consider using libraries that are FIPS 140-2 or FIPS 140-3 compliant for enhanced security assurance. Risk: Using insecure cryptographic libraries and functions can expose applications to significant security risks, such as data breaches and unauthorised access, compromising sensitive information.

title: Password Change
description: Enforce password change upon suspected account compromise.
guidance: Implement mechanisms to detect signs of account compromise, such as unusual login activity or multiple failed login attempts. Notify users promptly to change their passwords and provide guidance on creating strong, unique passwords. Consider integrating multi-factor authentication to enhance security. Risk: Failure to enforce password changes upon suspected account compromise increases the risk of prolonged unauthorised access, leading to potential data breaches and exploitation of systems.

title: Parameterised Interfaces
description: Use parameterised interfaces for database queries or system commands.
guidance: Parameterised interfaces such Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) libraries ensure that parameters used in database queries or system commands are properly sanitised and prevent injection attacks. Risk: Failure to use parameterised interfaces increases the vulnerability to SQL injection or command injection attacks, posing a significant risk of unauthorised access, data manipulation, or even potential system compromise.

title: Output Sanitisation
description: Sanitise all application outputs that will be used to render a HTML document.
guidance: Any application outputs that are returned to the requester and used to render a HTML document can lead to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks if they contain special characters that change the rendering of the HTML document by the browser. Risk: Lack of sanitisation for application outputs used in rendering HTML documents exposes the system to the risk of cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing malicious code execution in browsers.

title: Authentication Mechanism Rate-Limiting
description: Apply rate-limiting on all authentication mechanisms to deter brute-force attacks.
guidance: Consider rate-limiting to a maximum of 3 consecutive failed authentication attempts within 15 minutes or other reasonable rate limits. Time delays between log-on attempts reduce the risk of successful brute-forcing attacks. Bot mitigation tools such as CAPTCHA can further reduce this risk. Risk: Without rate-limiting, there's an increased risk of unauthorised access as attackers may exploit weak credentials through repeated login attempts.

title: Password Requirements
description: Where SSO or passwordless is not supported, verify that [ insert: param, as-5_prm_3 ] passwords are at least [ insert: param, as-5_prm_1 ] characters in length and [ insert: param, as-5_prm_2 ].
guidance: Latest NIST SP 800-63B guidelines found that password length is a primary factor in determining the strength of a password while composition and complexity rules provide marginal security benefits. Risk: Short or commonly used passwords increase the vulnerability to unauthorised access, potentially leading to compromised accounts and unauthorised activities on the system.

title: Password Salting and Hashing
description: Store passwords as salted hashes using a password hashing scheme that is resistant to offline attacks such as those described in NIST SP 800-63b. The salt should be: Generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator in accordance with industry standards; At least 32 bits long; and Randomly generated for each account.
guidance: Refer to NIST SP 800-90Ar1 for suitable pseudo-random number generators. Refer to NIST SP 800-63b Memorized Secret Verifiers section for suitable hashing schemes, including Argon2, scrypt, and PBKDF2. For application source code, use a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator function instead of an insecure one, such as crypto.randomBytes instead of Math.random in Node.js and java.security.SecureRandom.nextBytes instead of java.util.Random in Java. Risk: Without salting and hashing, in case of a data breach, exposed passwords can be easily extracted, leading to potential compromise of accounts and sensitive information.

title: Access Control Check Enforcement
description: Perform access control checks on all authenticated requests.
guidance: Utilise authorisation filters or middleware to force all authenticated requests to undergo access control checks. Risk: Failure to perform access control checks on authenticated requests increases the risk of unauthorised access to sensitive data or functionalities, potentially leading to data breaches and misuse of system resources.

title: Secrets Management
description: Securely store secrets in an appropriate secrets management solution with access control enforcement, encryption, and monitoring.
guidance: Secrets include API keys, access keys, and other static credentials. Do not store secrets unencrypted in source code or configuration files. Store secrets in cloud-native solutions like AWS Secrets Manager and Azure Key Vault or cloud-agnostic solutions like HashiCorp Vault and CyberArk Conjur. For SaaS or platforms, ensure that secrets are stored in an appropriate solution. For example, use GitHub Actions secrets instead of variables. Risk: Exposure of sensitive information and unauthorised access to system credentials may occur if application secrets are stored insecurely or hard-coded in source code.

title: Content Security Policy (CSP)
description: Set minimally permissive CSP response headers to mitigate cross-site scripting attacks.
guidance: Utilise the relevant fetch directives such as default-src, script-src, style-src, connect-src, img-src, media-src and object-src to prevent loading of scripts from malicious sources. Refer to the OWASP Secure Headers Project Best Practices for recommended header values. Risk: Without minimally permissive Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, the risk of cross-site scripting attacks, leading to unauthorised script execution and potential data theft, is increased.

title: Responsive Web Design
description: Adopt Responsive Web Design for web-based digital services. If specific content is deemed unsuitable for mobile devices, disable mobile device access, and clearly explain why the content or service is disabled and how it can be accessed.
guidance: A significant amount of web traffic comes from mobile devices. Responsive Web Design allows for optimised browsing experience on devices with different screen sizes.

title: Site Search
description: Provide a site search function for multi-page websites. Not required for mobile applications, transactional services, or websites where search is the service offered.
guidance: Search is a known and effective alternative to navigation for users who know what they are looking for.

title: Support multiple languages
description: Provide content in multiple languages to accommodate language preferences.
guidance: Allowing end users to select their preferred language enhances usability and inclusivity, allowing broader access and understanding.

title: Clear and Concise Content
description: Write in a clear and concise manner that is easy to read and understand; Choose simple words that most people can understand.
guidance: Writing in a simple and concise manner allows more users with different backgrounds and language proficiency to understand your content.

title: Search Engine Optimisation
description: Implement Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) best practices to improve website search engine rankings and results. Not required for restricted-access services or experimental/beta services.
guidance: SEO increases the findability and reach of web content by helping search platforms effectively crawl your content and optimising the content displayed in search listings.

title: Consistent UI Design
description: Use a design system or style guide to maintain a consistent user interface design throughout the entire service.
guidance: Consistent design and placement of interface components improves usability by allowing end users to quickly learn interface patterns.

title: Mandatory and Optional Fields
description: Indicate if input fields are mandatory or optional. Not required for login pages asking for username and password.
guidance: Reduces completion time by allowing end users to skip unnecessary fields and increases completion rates by helping end users understand the effort required.

title: Log-in Indication
description: Prominently display the name or identifier of the individual associated with the account after login.
guidance: Provides a clear indication that the end user is logged into the right account. This is especially important for shared devices.

title: Contact Channels
description: Provide at least one contact channel for help or assistance.
guidance: Allow end users to contact the relevant parties if they require help or assistance. Reassures users by providing a clear method to acquire information or resolve issues.

title: Backup
description: Backup all important data and systems at least every [ insert: param, br-1_prm_1 ] day(s), and store backups in a secure and separate location.
guidance: Use default CSP-managed backup services (AWS Backup, Azure Backup, GCP Backup and DR Service). Store backups separately from primary data with encryption-at-rest. For SaaS, ensure provider can restore last backup. Risk: Without regular backups stored in a secure and separate location, there is an increased risk of data loss, system failures, and extended downtime in the event of accidental deletion, hardware failures, or malicious attacks.

parameters.description: The time period in days for backup.

title: Recovery Testing
description: Conduct testing of recovery processes at least every [ insert: param, br-2_prm_1 ] day(s) to ensure their effectiveness.
guidance: Each test should verify the system's ability to fully restore all data and services. Risk: Failure to regularly test recovery processes may result in ineffective response during actual incidents, increasing the risk of prolonged downtime, data loss, and compromised business continuity in the event of a disaster or system failure.

parameters.description: The time period in days for recovery testing.

title: Backup Retention
description: Prevent backups from being modified or deleted for [ insert: param, br-3_prm_1 ] day(s) or as stipulated in the agency's data retention policies.
guidance: Use S3 Object Lock or Azure Blob Storage with immutability enabled to enforce time-based retention policies. Risk: Lack of prevention measures against the modification or deletion of backups for the specified duration increases the risk of data loss, unauthorised alterations, and potential inability to recover from incidents, compromising the integrity and availability of critical information.

parameters.description: The time period in days of backup retention.

title: Disaster Recovery Plan
description: Develop, maintain, and regularly test a disaster recovery plan that ensures critical functions and data can be restored within the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) as determined by business requirements and risk assessments.
guidance: Plan should include defined roles/responsibilities, step-by-step recovery procedures, communication protocols, and integration with business continuity planning. Assess effectiveness during disaster recovery exercises. Risk: Absence of a comprehensive disaster recovery plan increases the risk of prolonged system downtime, data loss, and inability to maintain business continuity in the event of a disaster, potentially leading to significant financial losses and damage to organisational reputation.

title: Business Continuity Plan
description: Develop a business continuity plan.
guidance: Refer to the Cyber Security Agency's Cybersecurity Toolkit for IT Teams for a business continuity plan template. Risk: Failure to develop a Business Continuity Plan may result in prolonged system downtime, loss of critical data, and diminished organisational resilience during disruptive events, increasing the risk of financial and reputational damage.

title: Business Continuity Exercise
description: Conduct a business continuity exercise at least every [ insert: param, br-6_prm_1 ] day(s) to test the effectiveness of the business continuity plan.
guidance: Testing can include checklists, tabletop exercises, and simulations based on the business continuity plan. Risk: Failure to conduct regular business continuity exercises may lead to unpreparedness during an actual disruption, increasing response times, operational impact, and the risk of ineffective recovery, ultimately jeopardising business operations and stakeholder trust.

parameters.description: The time period in days of business continuity exercise frequency.

title: Cryptographic Key Establishment
description: Use industry-standard cryptographic key establishment schemes and key derivation methods.
guidance: Risk: Insecure cryptographic key establishment can lead to weak or broken encryption.

title: Cryptographic Key Rotation
description: Rotate cryptographic keys every [insert: param, ck-2_prm_1] days.
guidance: Risk: Failing to rotate cryptographic keys increases the risk of broken encryption.

parameters.description: The time period in days of cryptographic key rotation frequency.

title: Cryptographic Key Management
description: Implement cryptographic key management processes to ensure cryptographic keys are well-managed and safeguarded throughout their lifecycle.
guidance: Risk: Inadequate key management increase the risk of unauthorised access, data breaches, and compromised cryptographic operations due to poorly managed or safeguarded keys.

title: Cryptographic Key Storage
description: Securely store cryptographic keys and implement strict access controls based on the principle of least privilege.
guidance: Risk: Inadequate key storage and access controls can lead to unauthorised key access and potential data breaches.

title: Unique Base Container Image Tags
description: Use unique base container image tags instead of rolling tags.
guidance: Avoid latest tag or other rolling tags to minimize unintended changes during subsequent builds. Digest SHA provides unique identifier if no tag assigned at build time. Risk: Using unique tags reduces risk of unintentional updates, inconsistencies, and security vulnerabilities in containerized environments.

title: Container Workload Segmentation
description: Segregate container workloads to help contain attacks through isolation.
guidance: Create Kubernetes namespaces or similar segmentation controls to isolate workloads, services, or projects. Risk: Without workload separation, increased lateral movement and compromise risk.

title: Container Runtime Security
description: Detect and remediate changes to running containers with container runtime protection tools.
guidance: Runtime tools (AWS EKS Protection, Microsoft Defender for Containers, Falco) monitor threats and changes. Isolate vulnerable instances for investigation and replace with patched images. Replace frequently with uncompromised images until patch release. These replace Malware Protection and EDR in container environments. Risk: Failure to detect and remediate runtime changes increases risk of unnoticed compromises and unauthorized alterations.

title: Minimal Base Container Images
description: Build container images with minimal base images.
guidance: Use minimal images such as alpine, scratch, wolfi, and distroless as base to reduce attack surface. Risk: Minimal base images reduce attack surface, vulnerabilities, and resource overhead, minimizing security exploit risk.

title: Runtime Container Secrets
description: Provide secrets and sensitive data to the container at runtime instead of image build time.
guidance: Ensure no secrets (TLS keys, cloud credentials, SSH keys, database passwords) embedded in image using Docker secrets or podman-secret-create. Risk: Runtime secret provisioning reduces exposure risk and enhances security through independent secret management.

title: Non-Privileged Container User
description: Create a non-root user and set it as the default user in the container image build instructions.
guidance: Ensure non-root user has minimal permissions required to run container. Risk: Failure to use non-root user increases vulnerability risk, as root privileges may lead to host system compromise.

title: Dockerfile Linting
description: Lint Dockerfiles before building container images.
guidance: Use linters like Hadolint to check Dockerfile instructions and flag best practice violations. Ensure linting runs in CI pipelines. Risk: Without linting, increased risk of syntax errors, misconfigurations, and security vulnerabilities.

title: Read-Only Container Root Filesystem
description: Configure the container root filesystem to be read-only during runtime, except for designated non-persistent storage locations or mounted volumes for stateful storage (e.g., caches, service data).
guidance: Use security policies (e.g., readonlyRootFilesystem for Kubernetes) to prevent root filesystem writes. Apply patches by rebuilding images. Use tmpfs mounts for temporary filesystems. Risk: Failure to enforce read-only filesystem increases tampering risk and compromise potential.

title: Container Image Scanning
description: Scan container images in the [ insert: param, cs-7_prm_1 ] for known vulnerabilities.
guidance: Tools like Amazon Inspector, Trivy, Grype scan for known vulnerabilities. Configure automatic, continuous scanning and block deployment of critical/high severity images. Risk: Failure to scan increases risk of deploying insecure images and exposing infrastructure to known exploits.

parameters.description: The location where container image scanning occurs.

title: Private Container Image Registries
description: Host built container images in private container registries.
guidance: Use only private registries (e.g., Amazon ECR private) since images may contain proprietary code or sensitive information. Risk: Private registries reduce exposure, minimize unauthorized access risk, and maintain image distribution control.

title: Container Orchestrator API Access Control
description: Disable public access to Container Orchestrator API endpoints from the internet.
guidance: Restrict API endpoints (Kubernetes API Server) to specific address ranges or use CSP features like disabling endpoint public access and Private Clusters. Risk: Public API endpoint exposure increases risk of unauthorized access, exploitation, and infrastructure compromise.

title: Separate hosting
description: Physically separate Government resources from non-Government resources.
guidance: For on-premise environments, ensure government resources are physically stored and secured separately from non-government resources. Risk: Violating this control can subject government data and systems to access risks leading to compromised systems and data.

title: Physical Access Controls
description: Implement physical access controls to prohibit unauthorised access to the hosting environment or network rooms.
guidance: Measures include: a) personnel security clearance and checks; b) continuous monitoring; c) immediate security response; d) strong authentication card access systems; e) 24/7 guards; f) restrict unauthorized devices; g) intrusion detection systems; h) CCTV monitoring. Risk: Violating this control can subject government data and systems to access risks leading to compromised systems and data.

title: Data Residency
description: Enforce data residency of [ insert: param, dp-1_prm_2 ] data in [ insert: param, dp-1_prm_1 ].
guidance: Risk: Failure to enforce data residency in the appropriate country may lead to legal and regulatory compliance issues, privacy concerns, and potential unauthorised access or storage of sensitive data outside the jurisdiction.

parameters.description: The country the data resides in.
The type of data that should have enforced data residency.

title: Data at Rest Encryption
description: Encrypt data at rest.
guidance: Many cloud service provider services encrypt data at rest by default but this should be confirmed and validated depending on service usage. Risk: Without encrypting data at rest, there's increased risk of unauthorised access and data exposure from physical theft, unauthorised storage media access, or compromised security controls.

title: Data in Transit Encryption
description: Encrypt data in transit.
guidance: While some CSP services transparently encrypt data in transit at the network layer, data at the application layer should be encrypted using protocols such as Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Secure Socket Layer (SSL). Risk: Failure to encrypt data in transit increases risk of unauthorised interception and eavesdropping, potentially leading to data breaches and compromise of sensitive information during transmission.

title: Central Cloud Tenant Management
description: Implement a centralised cloud tenant management structure for [ insert: param, dp-4_prm_1 ] using [ insert: param, dp-4_prm_2 ].
guidance: Consider services like AWS Organizations, GCP Organizations, or Azure Management Groups for centralised management. Implement appropriate landing zone frameworks, consistent policies, centralised logging, and tagging strategies. Risk: Lack of centralised cloud tenant management can lead to inconsistent security policies, reduced visibility, and increased difficulty managing and securing cloud resources across the organisation.

parameters.description: The systems to be hosted on a central tenant.
The central tenant management structure.

title: Sanitisation
description: Sanitise all hardware that stores data at rest. Shred or incinerate data storage meant for retirement.
guidance: Use industry standards such as a) Peter Gutmann Secure Deletion; b) Bruce Schneier Algorithm c) US Department of Defence's Standards (DoD 5220.22-M). Risk: Violating this control can expose government data to unauthorised users.

title: Witness Sanitisation and Destruction of Storage Devices
description: Witness the sanitisation and destruction process to ensure data is removed from storage.
guidance: Establish a SOP to ensure sanitisation and destruction are witnessed by an agency staff. Risk: Ensuring storage devices are sanitised or destroyed will eliminate the possibility of unauthorised or unintended data retention.

title: Data Loss Prevention
description: Implement data loss prevention mechanisms that monitor data flows, detect sensitive data transfers, and block unauthorised sharing of sensitive data.
guidance: Where possible, use built-in solutions such as Microsoft Purview or Google Workspace data loss prevention rules. Regularly review and update policies to adapt to evolving threats. Risk: Failure to implement data loss prevention measures increases risk of unauthorised data exfiltration, accidental data leaks, and data breaches, compromising sensitive information and organisational integrity.

title: Data Classification Disclosure
description: For internal applications serving public officers, specify the highest permitted security and sensitivity classification for input data, such as text, audio, or multimedia/file uploads, in the system's user interface and guides.
guidance: Indicate with a clear message, either at or near the input field, the relevant data classification that may be used with the system. Risk: Users not informed of maximum allowed data classification may submit sensitive information the system is not permitted to process, risking data breaches and legal violations.

title: Overseas-hosted GenAI API services
description: Use only up to RESTRICTED and SENSITIVE NORMAL data with GenAI API services served by models hosted overseas.
guidance: Verify data classification with data owner before using the data with overseas GenAI API services. Ensure that these API services are accessed only via environments authorised for up to RESTRICTED and SENSITIVE NORMAL data. Risk: Primary data is at greater legal, privacy, and exfiltration risk when in transit and processed by GenAI API services hosted in other countries.

title: Singapore-hosted GenAI API services
description: Use only up to CONFIDENTIAL and SENSITIVE HIGH data with GenAI API services served by models hosted in Singapore.
guidance: Verify data classification with data owner before using the data with Singapore-hosted GenAI API services. Ensure that these API services are accessed only via environments authorised for up to CONFIDENTIAL and SENSITIVE HIGH data. Check documentation for whether cross-region inferencing or overseas processing occurs under certain conditions. Risk: Primary data carries legal, privacy, and exfiltration risk when in transit and processed by GenAI API services hosted in Singapore.

title: Non-logging and non-training Agreement
description: Obtain a legally-binding commitment from the GenAI API service provider that states that they do not log, store, nor retain input and output data, and that no input and output data are used for training GenAI models. Prompt caching (i.e. temporarily storing responses to frequently used prompts) is exempt from the above restriction on logging, storing, or retaining data, provided the cache time-to-live (TTL) is ≤ 24 hours.
guidance: Ensure that the agreement covers all endpoints, parameters, outputs and models in use. Using GenAI API services provided by GCC 2.0 satisfies this control. Risk: Without a legally binding agreement, the GenAI service provider can access primary data or logs through automated or manual checks that can expose classified data, or they may use the data for further training of their GenAI models.

title: Data classification for self-hosted GenAI models
description: Ensure that GenAI models are hosted in an environment that can host the highest data classification of government data contained in the system that the model is deployed in.
guidance: Refer to relevant IM8 SSPs for controls that need to be met before hosting government data of a given data classification in that environment (e.g. in a Singapore-hosted GCC environment.) Risk: Using GenAI models with data that is more classified than what its environment is permitted to hold may open up cybersecurity vulnerabilities for attackers to exfiltrate classified data.

title: GenAI model formats and loaders
description: Use approved formats (such as [ insert: param, ga-5_prm_1 ]) when using any open-weights GenAI models. Use approved loaders (such as [ insert: param, ga-5_prm_2 ]) to load open-weights GenAI models.
guidance: Update GenAI model loaders frequently to hinder attacks. Risk: Insecure model formats or loaders have been shown to be potential threat vectors that may allow for arbitrary code execution. Failure to use more secure formats or loaders may result in potential unauthorised access to the system.

parameters.description: An example list of approved model formats.
An example list of approved model loaders.

title: File upload safeguards
description: Implement file upload safeguards if file uploads are enabled in the system.
guidance: Examples of safeguards include but are not limited to: (1) Implementing Data Loss Protection ("DLP") tools to monitor document uploads, (2) Disabling bulk or batch file uploads, such as by preventing users from selecting multiple files with a single action, or by requiring users to confirm the data security/sensitivity classification of each file individually before uploading, (3) Prompting users who upload excessively large files to review file contents and their collective data security/sensitivity classification. Risk: Enabling file uploads in a generative AI application creates two key risks: (a) the possibility of sensitive data leaks if models are prompted to reveal information from uploaded files, and (b) the risk of exceeding permitted data classification levels — either by uploading multiple files without reassessing their collective classification, or by inadvertently uploading documents with a higher classification level due to human error.

title: Evaluation of GenAI accuracy, safety, and output quality
description: Test the accuracy, safety, and quality of the GenAI application's outputs, with clearly defined metrics, test scenarios, and criteria.
guidance: Determine the adequate level of accuracy, safety, and output quality for your application. Develop tests to assess outputs on these dimensions. The complexity and structure of these tests should be tailored to the risk profile of your application. Document this approach and measure & monitor results after relevant model, prompt, and dependency updates. Risk: Failure to evaluate models, prompts, and their dependencies (such as tool integrations and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems) can result in low-quality outputs after updates or configuration changes.

title: Inform users about GenAI risks and limitations
description: Require users to explicitly acknowledge the risk of inaccurate or fabricated outputs (hallucinations), such as selecting a checkbox or clicking on an 'I Agree' button before the application can be accessed.
guidance: Include clauses about the risk of inaccurate / fabricated outputs in your Terms of Use. Indicate prominently in your application about the possibility of inaccurate or fabricated outputs. Ensure that educational materials, such as documentation, guides, playbooks, or workshops, highlight responsible use and best practices for users of the GenAI system. Risk: Uninformed users may trust inaccurate model-generated outputs.

title: Security Awareness Training
description: Conduct security awareness training for all employees that operate and manage the system every [ insert: param, hr-1_prm_1 ] months.
guidance: Develop training covering: (a) Relevant laws, regulations, codes of practice, policies, standards, guidelines and procedures (b) Phishing and social engineering awareness (c) Incident reporting procedures (d) Secure handling of sensitive information. Also utilize posters, emails to provide regular and timely communication covering cybersecurity awareness messages and prevailing threats, impacts and mitigations.

parameters.description: The frequency at which security awareness training should be conducted.

title: Security Screening of Employees
description: Conduct security screening of employees that operate and manage the system, during their hiring phase.
guidance: Consider engaging reputable 3rd party screening companies to conduct background checks before extending employment offers.

title: Employee Termination Process
description: Develop and document a process for the secure termination of employees.
guidance: Process should include: (1) Deprovisioning accounts promptly before terminating employees to reduce opportunity for damage (2) Conducting exit interviews to ensure understanding of ongoing confidentiality obligations (3) Ensuring all issued equipment is returned and inventoried (4) Secure disposal of employee's data and removal of access rights (5) Notification to relevant stakeholders.

title: Restricted Administrator Privileges
description: Restrict administrator privileges by disabling remote login for the root/administrator user and restricting sudo/administrators group access.

title: Least Functionality
description: Disable or remove unnecessary functions, system ports, protocols, software, and services on the host.

title: Host System Hardening
description: Harden the host configuration with reference to industry standards.

title: Remote Administration

title: Security Monitoring and Alerting
description: Configure security monitoring to identify potential security violations or breaches and send automated alerts, and respond to them accordingly.

title: Network and System Component Segmentation
description: Segment and isolate system components into separate physical and logical networks or environments based on their security requirements and risk levels.
guidance: Deploy firewalls, security groups, and API gateways for segmentation. Implement tiered cloud architecture with public-facing services isolated from private backend systems. Consider micro-segmentation based on workload sensitivity. Risk: Failure to segregate private and public resources within distinct subnets in a virtual network increases the risk of unauthorised access to sensitive data, as private resources may be exposed to the public internet, compromising the overall security of the infrastructure.

title: Private Network Connectivity
description: Implement strong access controls, encryption, and logging for remote developer, maintainer, or administrator access to private network resources.
guidance: Use strong authentication and MFA. Inspect gateway traffic, terminate connections in dedicated segments, implement strong encryption, restrict device access, avoid perpetual connections, re-authenticate periodically, enforce failed authentication lockouts, and disable split tunnelling. Risk: Weak private network security may expose the network to malicious activities, jeopardising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of critical resources.

title: Alerts on Firewall Configuration Changes
description: Generate alerts to inform appointed administrators on changes to firewall rules, including the enabling or disabling of rules.
guidance: Implement real-time alerts for firewall rule creation, deletion, modification, enabling/disabling, and unusual resource utilization spikes. Risk: Any unintended changes to firewall rules can significantly lower the perimeter defence of a network.

title: Access Restrictions on CSP Resources Outside Virtual Network
description: Restrict access to CSP resources outside of a virtual network (e.g., Lambda, DynamoDb, API Gateways, S3, CloudFront) using access controls or application layer authorisation.
guidance: Apply resource-specific restrictions (IAM policies for DynamoDB, Lambda authorizers for API Gateway, IAM policies and public access blocks for S3). Use private API endpoints when needed. Risk: Lack of access restrictions raises the risk of unauthorised access, data exposure, and potential misuse of critical services, compromising the overall security posture.

title: Deny by Default - Allow by Exception
description: Deny network communications traffic by default and allow network communications traffic by exception at managed interfaces.
guidance: Configure network ACLs and security groups to deny all traffic initially. Allow only specific hosts/ports by exception. Consider whitelisting domains at application layer for egress. Risk: Without network access controls, there's an increased risk of unauthorised or malicious network access, leading to potential security breaches and compromise of system integrity.

title: Inter-Private Network Connectivity
description: Route network traffic between private networks without going through the internet.
guidance: Use AWS PrivateLink with VPC endpoints for unidirectional service access. Alternatively, use VPC peering or Transit Gateway for layer-3 IP connectivity between VPCs. Risk: When routing through the internet, there's an increased risk of man-in-the-middle and spoofing attacks. Allowing bidirectional access between networks without fine-grained access controls increases the risk of unauthorised access, potential data exfiltration, and compromise of network security compared to unidirectional access to specific resources.

title: Network and Application Layer Filtering
description: Filter direct traffic from the internet to protect against network and application layer attacks.
guidance: Deploy Web Application Firewall, Distributed Denial of Service Protection (e.g., AWS Shield), or Content Delivery Network (e.g., CloudFront) as appropriate. Risk: Lack of filtering for direct traffic from the internet exposes the system to the risk of network and application layer attacks, increasing the likelihood of unauthorised access, denial-of-service incidents, and compromise of sensitive data.

title: Valid and Trusted SSL/TLS Certificates
description: Ensure that deployed SSL/TLS certificates are: signed by a trusted root Certificate Authority; match the domain name of the service they are issued for; not expired; and not revoked.
guidance: Configure certificate manager with auto-renewal and pre-expiry alerts (e.g., AWS Certificate Manager) or automate separately. Risk: Using invalid SSL/TLS certificates introduces the risk of compromised encryption, man-in-the-middle attacks, and potential unauthorised access to sensitive information.

title: Secure Inter-Service Communication
description: Ensure communications between services are secure by making them authenticated, authorised and encrypted.
guidance: Design inter-service communications (databases, microservices) to be authenticated, authorised and encrypted via API gateways, proxies, private endpoint services, message queues, or service meshes. Log communications for detection and investigation. Risk: Failure to ensure secure communications between services increases the risk of unauthorised access, data breaches, and potential manipulation of sensitive information during transit.

title: Secure Cloud and On-Premises Connectivity
description: Route network traffic between on-premises systems and cloud systems through a secure intermediary.
guidance: Design secure communications via managed interfaces with boundary protections rather than direct connectivity. Use API gateways, application proxies, or private endpoint services. Risk: Insecure connectivity between cloud and on-premises environments can lead to data breaches, unauthorised access, and compromise of both cloud and on-premises resources.

title: Intrusion Prevention System (IPS)/Intrusion Detection System (IDS)
description: Set up and configure an Intrusion Prevention System (IPS)/Intrusion Detection System (IDS) in the network.
guidance: Configure network or host IPS/IDS to detect malicious traffic to/from public or untrusted networks. Risk: Absence of network or host IPS or IDS in the network increases the likelihood of undetected intrusions, putting sensitive data and system integrity at risk.

title: Digital Service Review
description: Review digital services every [ insert: param, pr-1_prm_1 ] day(s). Shut down services that are no longer needed or fail to meet their intended objectives.
guidance: Review factors such as relevance, importance and usage rates of the service. Rationale: Services that are not effective incur unnecessary costs for the organisation.

title: Digital Service Registration
description: Register and implement WOGAA on all public facing digital services.
guidance: Registration includes registration of all public facing digital services, implementation of WOGAA tracking code, and enabling Sentiments. Only registration is required for SaaS and COTS products lacking customization options. Rationale: A centralised registry and tracking of digital services across Whole-of-Government facilitates central oversight and benchmarking of digital services.

title: Digital Service Availability
description: Make digital services available to users 24/7. Clearly communicate the operational hours if a service cannot be available 24/7.
guidance: Do not limit the availability of services to specific hours unless justified by operational or business requirements. Rationale: End users expect to have access to digital channels anytime excluding planned and unplanned downtime.

title: Notify of Scheduled Downtime
description: Provide notice of scheduled downtime at least [ insert: param, pr-4_prm_1 ] day(s) in advance.
guidance: Clearly communicate scheduled downtime using methods like maintenance banners and in-app notifications. Rationale: Awareness of scheduled downtime minimises disruption to users by allowing them to plan around it.

parameters.description: The time period in days to provide notice of schedule downtime.

title: Manage Broken Links
description: Establish processes to detect broken links, and address them within [ insert: param, pr-5_prm_1 ] day(s) from detection.
guidance: Use automated tools like WOGAA's broken link scanner to regularly scan for broken links. Rationale: Broken links affect content delivery and prevent end users from completing tasks.

parameters.description: The time period in days to address broken links.

title: Browser Compatibility
description: Ensure web-based services are compatible with the latest major versions of at least [ insert: param, pr-6_prm_1 ] widely used web browsers, based on usage statistics.
guidance: Regularly test your service on the latest two major versions of popular browsers such as Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. Rationale: Browser incompatibility can cause layout bugs and other functional issues.

parameters.description: The number of web browsers.

title: Optimise Load Times
description: Ensure that page load time of web-based services is [ insert: param, pr-7_prm_1 ] second(s) or less.
guidance: Track or regularly test and optimise performance using tools like WOGAA and Google PageSpeed Insights. Rationale: Long page load times frustrate end users and lead to longer transaction times and increased abandonment rate.

parameters.description: The time period in seconds for page load times.

title: Multi-AZ Deployment
description: Deploy the system in [ insert: param, rs-1_prm_1 ] availability zones (AZs) within the region.
guidance: Utilize cloud-native services for load-balancing and auto-scaling across multiple AZs. Implement health checks and automated failover mechanisms to redirect traffic. Ensure data is replicated across multiple AZs. Risk: Failure to deploy services across multiple availability zones increases the risk of extended service outages due to a single point of failure.

parameters.description: The number of availability zones to deploy to.

title: Dynamic Resource Scaling
description: Implement and utilise dynamic resource scaling techniques in the system.
guidance: Resource optimization techniques like load balancing and auto-scaling should maximize utilization and minimize idle resources by adjusting to real-time demand fluctuations, per the AWS Well-Architected Framework's 'Reliability' pillar. Risk: Failure to implement dynamic resource scaling may lead to inefficient resource utilisation and potential service degradation during spikes in demand. This can lead to system outages during peak loads, reducing overall system performance and reliability.

title: Load Testing
description: Perform load testing every [ insert: param, rs-3_prm_1 ] days.
guidance: Load testing should be conducted on a replica of the production system. The load should mimic real user traffic. Risk: Inadequate load testing may lead to unexpected system failures during periods of high demand, leading to service interruptions.

parameters.description: The frequency at which load testing should be performed.

title: Code Repository
description: Manage the codebase in a central code repository with version control.
guidance: Use common internal platforms that provide Git repository services. Risk: Absence of centralised code repository and version control increases the risk of code inconsistencies, loss of code history, and difficulties in collaboration.

title: Commit Signing
description: Configure the code repository to reject unsigned commits.
guidance: Use GitLab's push rules, GitHub's branch protection rules or similar controls to reject unsigned commits on push. Risk: Allowing unsigned commits introduces risk of unauthorised or malicious code changes, compromising software development integrity.

title: Peer Review
description: Require peer review and approval by a designated reviewer before merging into the default branch.
guidance: Use GitLab's protected branch and merge request settings, GitHub's branch protection settings or similar controls. Risk: Without peer review, increased risk of undetected coding errors, security vulnerabilities, and consistency challenges.

title: Dependency Manifest Version Pinning
description: Pin direct and transitive dependency versions in the application's dependency manifest.
guidance: Dependency manifests such as package-lock.json for npm and Pipfile.lock for pipenv allow pinning dependency versions. Risk: Failure to pin versions may lead to version drift, compatibility issues, security vulnerabilities, and unpredictability.

title: Build and Release Process
description: Use a consistent build and release process that generates a record of how the release artefact was built and deployed.
guidance: Consider automated tools like CI/CD Pipelines, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), and scripts enabling signing and validation of build artefacts. Risk: Inconsistent releases may lead to configuration drift, increased errors, and unapproved changes.

title: Dependency Installation during Deployment
description: Only install pinned versions in the manifest when installing dependencies during deployment.
guidance: Use package manager commands like npm ci for npm and pipenv sync for pipenv ensuring only manifest-specified versions install. Risk: Failure to install pinned versions increases risk of unforeseen changes, compatibility issues, and security vulnerabilities.

title: Software Artefact Signing
description: Sign software artefacts such as code and container images using a trusted source during build.
guidance: Use tools like Cosign or AWS Signer to sign and verify code. Risk: Unsigned code and container images risk tampering, impersonation, and malicious code injection during build.

title: Software Artefact Signature Verification
description: Verify the signatures of code and artefacts before deployment or runtime.
guidance: Implement a signature verification step such as a pipeline stage or Kubernetes Admission Controller. Risk: Without signature verification, increased risk of deploying tampered or malicious software.

title: Internal Code Collaboration and Sharing
description: Share source code internally to enhance code quality, accelerate innovation, and improve problem-solving efficiency.
guidance: Adopt InnerSource practices for internal collaboration utilising Git platforms. Evaluate code suitability for sharing, considering confidential algorithms or sensitive data. Risk: Restricting repositories to closed source results in duplicated efforts, hindered learning, and missed vulnerabilities.

title: Push Protection for Secrets
description: Configure the code repository to prevent secrets from being pushed to the repository.
guidance: Use GitLab's push rules or GitHub's push protection to reject secrets on push. Risk: Failure to configure the code repository to prevent secrets from being pushed introduces the risk of inadvertent exposure, unauthorised access, and potential misuse of sensitive information, compromising the security of the codebase and associated systems.

title: Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC)
description: Implement and maintain a secure software development lifecycle based on an industry-standard or organisation-defined framework, integrating security practices throughout all phases of application design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance.
guidance: Outline a framework that defines roles, responsibilities, and accountability for security throughout the SSDLC. Existing frameworks include NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF), OWASP Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM), and Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Risk: Failure to implement a comprehensive secure software development lifecycle increases the risk of introducing vulnerabilities throughout the development process, potentially leading to security breaches, data leaks, and compromised system integrity in production environments.

title: Default Branch Push Permissions
description: Configure the code repository to prevent pushes (including force pushes) to the default branch.
guidance: Use GitLab's protected branch and merge request settings or GitHub's branch protection settings to enforce this. Risk: Without configuring the code repository to prevent pushes, including force pushes, to the default branch, there's an increased risk of unintentional or malicious changes, potential loss of code history, and compromised version control, impacting the integrity and reliability of the software development process.

title: Continuous Integration (CI) Tests
description: Require Continuous Integration (CI) tests to pass before merging into the default branch.
guidance: Use GitLab's protected branch and merge request settings or GitHub's branch protection settings to enforce this. Risk: Failing to require passing Continuous Integration (CI) tests before merging into the default branch increases the risk of introducing faulty code, potential regressions, and compromise of code quality.

title: Static Analysis
description: Set up a static analysis job in the [insert: param, sd-4_prm_1], and remediate or risk accept true positive vulnerability findings before deploying to production.
guidance: Static analysis tools (such as SAST or IaC security scanners) check source code for common vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. By running static analysis tools earlier in the DevSecOps cycle, vulnerabilities can be detected and prevented from being deployed to production. Risk: Without setting up static analysis in the CI/CD pipeline for each merge request and addressing true positive vulnerability findings, there is an increased risk of deploying insecure code to the production branch, potentially leading to security breaches and compromise of the overall system.

parameters.description: The location where static analysis occurs.

title: Dependency Scanning
description: Schedule a scan at least every [insert: param, sd-5_prm_1] day(s) in the [insert: param, sd-5_prm_2] to identify the use of vulnerable software libraries.
guidance: Dependency scanning checks the source code for dependencies with known vulnerabilities. By running scans regularly using bots or software composition analysis (SCA) tools, vulnerabilities arising from outdated dependencies can be quickly detected and patched. Software composition analysis can be performed using tools such as Gitlab, Nexus IQ, or their equivalent, with output in a common SBOM format such as SPDX or CycloneDX. Risk: Failing to schedule regular dependency scanning to identify vulnerable software libraries and address findings in a timely manner increases the risk of deploying applications with known vulnerabilities, potentially exposing the system to security exploits and compromise.

parameters.description: The time period in days of dependency scanning frequency.
The location where dependency scanning occurs.

title: Secret Detection
description: Set up secret detection in the [insert: param, sd-6_prm_1] and remediate true positives within [insert: param, sd-6_prm_2] day(s).
guidance: Ensure that the exposed secret is revoked and purged from the Git history. Risk: Without setting up secret detection and addressing true positive findings promptly, there's an increased risk of exposing sensitive information, potential unauthorised access, and compromised security.

parameters.description: The location where secret detection occurs.
Number of days within which to remediate a secret detection true positive.

title: CI Environment Variable Secrets Management
description: Protect environment variable secrets used in CI jobs by limiting them to protected pipelines and masking them in job logs.
guidance: Use GitLab's CI/CD variable security settings or GitHub's encrypted secrets with the add-mask workflow command. Risk: Failing to protect environment variable secrets in CI jobs by limiting them to protected pipelines and masking them in job logs increases the risk of unauthorised access and exposure of sensitive information.

title: Deployment Environment Segregation
description: Segregate production and non-production environments including applications, services, data, secrets, roles, and networks.
guidance: Achieve segregation using separate cloud tenant accounts for environments such as production, development, test, and staging. Account segregation enhances security by limiting exposure, simplifies resource and cost management, maintains configuration integrity, facilitates compliance and auditing and streamlines operational tasks. Deploy and operate environments as similarly as possible to enhance debugging and time-to-market. Risk: Failure to segregate production and non-production environments increases the risk of unauthorised access, data leaks, and denial of service attacks, as compromises in non-production environments may lead to cascading impacts on production systems.

title: Dynamic Analysis
description: Implement dynamic analysis testing in the [insert: param, sd-9_prm_1], and address or risk-accept all identified vulnerabilities before deploying to production.
guidance: Dynamic analysis tools (such as DAST, IAST, or fuzzing tools) test applications in runtime conditions to identify vulnerabilities that may not be apparent in static code. Integrate these tools into your CI/CD pipeline to automatically scan applications in a controlled environment. Ensure that the analysis covers various attack vectors, including input validation, authentication mechanisms, and API endpoints. Regularly update and tune your dynamic analysis tools to detect emerging threats and vulnerabilities. Risk: Failure to perform dynamic analysis in a controlled environment before production deployment increases the risk of undetected runtime vulnerabilities, potentially leading to security breaches, data leaks, and compromised system integrity in the production environment.

parameters.description: The location where static analysis occurs.

description: Run regular [insert: param, st-1_prm_1] vulnerability assessment scans for eligible hosts at least every [insert: param, st-1_prm_2] day(s).

title: Cloud Security Posture Management

description: Establish a public reporting channel for disclosing vulnerabilities in public-facing systems via [insert: param, st-3_prm_1].
